registry.title: Does noticing a change mean adjusting to it?
registry.hypothesis: Noticing that something changed and getting back to correct behavior are different skills, and how the agent remembers decides which one it is good at.
registry.design: The world's rules genuinely change six times on a fixed schedule. After each change, three clocks start: how long until the agent stops giving the now-wrong answer, until it first gives the new right answer, and until it gets it right twice in a row. The agents differ only in how they remember.

parameters.changes: 6 real rule changes, evenly spaced after a 20-step warmup
parameters.agents compared: a lookup-table baseline, plus the same LLM with no memory, a 40-step transcript, self-written notes (rewritten every 10 steps), or extracted procedures
parameters.latency units: tries on the affected tasks, not raw steps

dependent: the gap between detection and recovery

predictions.claim: recovery lag differs between memory architectures on the same seeds
